text: Pig housing (ទ្រុងជ្រូក) should protect against heat, heavy rain, flooding, injury, predators, and disease while providing clean water, feeding space, drainage, and manure management. During the wet season, drainage is critical -- muddy pens and standing water worsen hygiene and disease risk. During the dry season, heat stress is the major concern since pigs can't sweat effectively -- shade, airflow, abundant clean water, and practical cooling matter most. Biosecurity (ជីវសុវត្ថិភាព) is especially important for ASF and CSF prevention: avoid unnecessary mixing of pigs from different sources, obtain new pigs from known-health-status sources where possible, and keep new pigs separate and monitored before joining the group (isolation period per veterinary guidance, not a fixed number). CRITICAL: untreated food waste containing pork or other animal products should NEVER be fed to pigs -- this is a serious disease-transmission pathway, distinct from plant-based feed materials which may be usable after assessment. People, footwear, vehicles, equipment, and contaminated materials can all introduce pathogens; clean equipment routinely, not just after disease appears. If pigs show rapidly spreading illness, sudden unexplained deaths, high fever, severe weakness, or hemorrhagic signs, stop unnecessary movement immediately, separate affected animals, and seek veterinary help -- do not advise selling or moving apparently healthy pigs from an affected group, since that can spread disease further. Do not guess a pig breed for Preah Vihear -- record what the farmer actually has.
